cards.title: Introduction to JWT
cards.content:
JSON Web Tokens (JWT) are an open, industry-standard RFC 7519 method for representing claims securely between two parties.

In a Flask application, JWTs are commonly used for stateless authentication, meaning the server does not need to store session data in a database.

cards.title: Anatomy of a JWT
cards.content:
A JWT consists of three parts separated by dots (.):

  • Header: Contains the type of token and the signing algorithm (e.g., HS256).
  • Payload: Contains the claims or user data (e.g., user ID, roles).
  • Signature: Used to verify that the sender of the token is who it says it is and to ensure the message wasn't changed along the way.

cards.title: Flask-JWT-Extended
cards.content:
To implement JWT in Flask, we typically use the Flask-JWT-Extended extension. It provides helpers to create tokens, protect routes, and manage user identities easily.

from flask_jwt_extended import JWTManager, create_access_token, jwt_required
